title: Compactified finite-level projection formula
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ have the chosen compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$, $f=pj$, with $j$ a quasi-compact open immersion and $p$ proper [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification]. Work on the small pro-etale sites in the fixed universes. Fix a sheaf of commutative rings $R_Y$ on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$, put $R_{\overline X}=p^{-1}R_Y$ and $R_X=j^{-1}R_{\overline X}$, and use the composite inverse-image identification for $f$. All categories are the ordinary uncompleted unbounded derived categories of these module sheaves and the operations are those of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Let $E\in D(R_X)$ be arbitrary and let $Q\in D(R_Y)$ be site-perfect: locally on every site object it has a bounded representative with terms direct summands of finite free coefficient sheaves [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. No common global bound is assumed.

Write $c_{j,p}:Lf^*Q\xrightarrow{\sim}Lj^*Lp^*Q$ for the composition comparison [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. The map $\pi_{p,j_!E,Q}$ is the adjoint of the derived counit tensored with $1_Q$, using the pullback-tensor comparison; this is the same formula as [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows], now for $Q$. Let $\alpha_{j,E,M}:j_!(E\otimes^L Lj^*M)\to j_!E\otimes^L M$ be the adjunction projection map, the transpose of the unit tensored with $Lj^*M$, with the normalization of [lemma-weil-pbc-projection-formula-open-piece]. For $M=Lp^*Q$ this map is invertible. Put
$$\theta_j=j_!(1_E\otimes c_{j,p}^{-1})\circ\alpha_{j,E,Lp^*Q}^{-1}.$$
Then the ordered composite
$$
(Rf_!^{(j,p)}E)\otimes^LQ=(Rp_*j_!E)\otimes^LQ
\xrightarrow{\pi_{p,j_!E,Q}}Rp_*(j_!E\otimes^LLp^*Q)
\xrightarrow{Rp_*\theta_j}Rp_*j_!(E\otimes^LLf^*Q)
=Rf_!^{(j,p)}(E\otimes^LLf^*Q)
$$
is an isomorphism. With $\rho_{p,j_!E,Q}=\pi_{p,j_!E,Q}^{-1}$, its inverse is
$$\rho_{p,j_!E,Q}\circ Rp_*(\theta_j^{-1}).$$
On each local strict-perfect representative, $\rho$ agrees with the signed-totalization inverse of [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows].

proof.text: The exact adjunction $j_!\dashv j^*$ is supplied by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], after identifying $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with $\overline X_{\mathrm{proet}}/X$ using [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. Its exact functors act termwise on the unbounded derived categories by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Their derived adjunction follows from [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general]: since both functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms, every arrow in its resolution diagrams is already an isomorphism after localization; evaluation at the identity quasi-isomorphism gives the representing cone and cocone. Its characterization sends the termwise unit and counit to their localization classes. For a localized open immersion, use its localized coefficient ring and its exact extension-by-zero/restriction pair in these same resolution diagrams; evaluation at the identity again identifies the derived unit and counit with their termwise classes. Thus the adjunction projection map $\alpha$ is globally defined for arbitrary $M$, by transposing the unit tensored with $Lj^*M$, and specializes to exactly the map whose inverse the open-piece statement names.

source.place: Tags 03DI/03DJ, lemma-extension-by-zero and lemma-extension-by-zero-exact; derived adjunction by the cited general theorem

proof.text:
Here is the localization comparison for $j_!$ needed below, including its normalization. For any object $W\to\overline X$ of the pro-etale site, set $W_X=X\times_{\overline X}W$. Write $v:W\to\overline X$, $v_X:W_X\to X$, $j_W:W_X\to W$, and $r_W=v^*$, $r_X=v_X^*$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] and [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change], $j_W$ is a quasi-compact open immersion. Together with the proper identity map of $W$ it gives the chosen compactification $(j_W,1_W)$ of [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification]. By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], the small sites of $W$ and $W_X$ are the respective slice sites, so the localized module operations used here are those for these schemes. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-restriction] to $v$ and the site object $X$ to obtain $j^*Rv_*\cong R(v_X)_*j_W^*$, with its counit-compatible normalization. The adjunctions in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] and step 1 give, naturally in $H$,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(r_Wj_!E,H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(E,j^*Rv_*H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(E,R(v_X)_*j_W^*H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(r_XE,j_W^*H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(j_{W!}r_XE,H).$$
The representing-object universal property therefore gives $r_Wj_!E\cong j_{W!}r_XE$. The map is the mate of the restriction square. Apply the displayed Hom chain to the identity: its adjunct is the restricted unit of $j_!\dashv j^*$, so this comparison carries that unit to the local unit. Using also the restriction-pullback and restriction-tensor comparisons in the restriction node, transposing the restricted unit tensored with $Lj^*M$ gives the local transpose. Hence restriction of $\alpha_{j,E,M}$ is precisely $\alpha_{j_W,r_XE,r_WM}$, rather than an unspecified isomorphism of its endpoints.

source.place: Proof, open-piece localization, expanded by the Hom adjunction calculation

proof.text: Put $A=j_!E$. For each object $V$ of $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$, choose a covering $\{V_i\to V\}$ and bounded finite-projective representatives $F_i^\bullet\simeq Q|_{V_i}$ using [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-restriction], restriction of $\pi_{p,A,Q}$ is the adjoint-of-counit map for the localized ringed morphism $p_i$ and $A|_{\overline X\times_YV_i}$. Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-projection-formula-totalization] to that ringed morphism, that arbitrary object, and $F_i^\bullet$. It says both composites of $\pi$ and $\rho$ are identities. Write $u_i:F_i^\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}Q|_{V_i}$, $a_i=1_{R(p_i)_*A_i}\otimes u_i$, and $b_i=R(p_i)_*(1_{A_i}\otimes Lp_i^*u_i)$, where $A_i$ is the restriction of $A$. Naturality of the counit and of the pullback-tensor comparison, followed by the adjunction bijection, gives $\pi_{p_i,A_i,Q|_{V_i}}a_i=b_i\pi_{p_i,A_i,F_i}$. Both $a_i$ and $b_i$ are isomorphisms because they are images of $u_i$ under functors. Thus $\pi_{p_i,A_i,Q|_{V_i}}=b_i\pi_{p_i,A_i,F_i}a_i^{-1}$ has inverse $a_i\rho_{p_i,A_i,F_i}b_i^{-1}$: the two products reduce respectively to $b_i(\pi_F\rho_F)b_i^{-1}=1$ and $a_i(\rho_F\pi_F)a_i^{-1}=1$. Hence each restriction of the global projection map is invertible. The local detection clause of the restriction node proves that the global $\pi_{p,A,Q}$ is invertible; define $\rho$ to be its inverse. Restriction of this global inverse is the specified local $\rho$, since functors preserve inverse equations and an inverse is unique. For a global strict-perfect representative this is the inverse of [lemma-weil-pbc-projection-formula-proper-piece]. The use of totalization on slices does not assume those slices satisfy an additional geometric properness theorem: totalization holds for any ringed morphism.

source.place: Proof, first arrow and proper-piece inverse pair; local detection replaces inverse gluing

proof.text: The same packages give the required local tests for the open arrow. For any object $T\to\overline X$, choose a strict-perfect covering of $Y$ and pull it back to $T$. Such a covering of $Y$ exists by applying [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package] to the final site object. The base-change functor in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] is covering-preserving, so the resulting objects $T_a$ cover $T$. On each $T_a$, the restriction-pullback comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-restriction] identifies $(Lp^*Q)|_{T_a}$ with the pullback of a bounded package. That pullback is a bounded finite-projective complex: the exact coefficient-identified pullback in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] sends $R_Y$ to the chosen source ring, sends finite sums to finite sums as a left adjoint, and sends $p_ri_r=1$ to the same splitting equation. It is computed termwise, so the bounded representative is valid. By step 2 the restriction of $\alpha_{j,E,Lp^*Q}$ is the normalized open adjunction projection map for this package and $E|_{X\times_{\overline X}T_a}$. The open-piece theorem [lemma-weil-pbc-projection-formula-open-piece] gives its inverse; hence each restricted $\alpha$ is invertible. Apply the local detection clause of the restriction node on $\overline X$ to conclude that $\alpha_{j,E,Lp^*Q}$ is globally invertible. Again its global inverse restricts to the local inverse by uniqueness, without a descent assertion for arbitrary derived morphisms.

source.place: Proof, strict-perfect cover and open-piece inverse pair; finite-free splittings pulled back termwise

proof.text: Apply the current statement of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] with $(Z,W,V)=(X,\overline X,Y)$, $(h,k)=(j,p)$ and $(R_Z,R_W,R_V)=(R_X,R_{\overline X},R_Y)$. These are sheaves of commutative rings: $R_Y$ is commutative by hypothesis, and its specified inverse images retain that ring identity. The two coefficient identifications are the defining equalities $R_{\overline X}=p^{-1}R_Y$ and $R_X=j^{-1}R_{\overline X}$; the identification for $f=pj$ is explicitly their composite as required by the cited statement. Thus $c_{j,p}:Lf^*Q\to Lj^*Lp^*Q$ is a canonical isomorphism. Therefore $\theta_j=j_!(1_E\otimes c_{j,p}^{-1})\alpha^{-1}$ is an isomorphism, with inverse $\alpha\,j_!(1_E\otimes c_{j,p})$. Applying the functor $Rp_*$ gives inverse arrows $b=Rp_*\theta_j$ and $b^{-1}=Rp_*(\theta_j^{-1})$, because a functor preserves composition and identities. This makes the shorthand $Lj^*Lp^*Q=Lf^*Q$ in the blueprint a typed isomorphism with the correct direction.

source.place: Proof, Lj*Lp*Q = Lf*Q, interpreted through the canonical comparison

proof.text:
Write $a=\pi_{p,j_!E,Q}$ and $a^{-1}=\rho_{p,j_!E,Q}$. By associativity and the inverse equations of steps 3 and 5,
$$(a^{-1}b^{-1})(ba)=a^{-1}(b^{-1}b)a=a^{-1}a=1,\qquad(ba)(a^{-1}b^{-1})=b(aa^{-1})b^{-1}=bb^{-1}=1.$$
Thus $ba$ has exactly the inverse stated. The equalities $Rf_!^{(j,p)}=Rp_*j_!$ at both endpoints are the definition in [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification]. This proves the assertion for all $E$, including unbounded $E$, without a uniform bound on the local packages.
